old_findings.note: The mulDiv expansions are unchanged (the conversion functions did not change).

regressions.decompiled: call asset.transfer(address recipient, uint256 amount) with: args Bytes(28, uint128(_param1 >> 32)), Bytes(4, uint32(_param1)), -_23 + _param3 - (mulmod(_param3, stor5, stor5 + 10**18) > 0)
regressions.old: call asset.transfer(address recipient, uint256 amount) with: args _param1, -_23 + _param3 - (mulmod(_param3, stor5, stor5 + 10**18) > 0)
regressions.source: SafeTransferLib.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, amount): the call data is built in scratch memory with the address at an unaligned offset
regressions.issue: The recipient argument, printed as _param1 in round 1, is now cut at a 32-byte boundary into a 28-byte and a 4-byte piece. The same split appears as a new finding in c00156 and as re-stores in c00162 and c00210.
regressions.rule: Merge adjacent byte pieces that are consecutive slices of one value (Bytes(28, v >> 32), Bytes(4, uint32(v)) with v < 2^160 is the word address(v)) before splitting call data into ABI arguments.

improvements: The authority.canCall call is named with arguments (caller, target, selector). The custom error 0xfb563026 is decoded in both functions (it was a raw memory revert), and unknownf6e715d0 returns Array(len=_28, ...) instead of raw words. Whole-byte hex is printed in def storage, and P2 2 -> 1.
notes: Diff of 302 lines, 4 changed functions, all read. calls, logs, requires, reverts and whiles are equal in number; the manage loop (the only source loop) changed only in variable form (the result-encoding loop uses mem[64] instead of _38).
summary: One medium regression: asset.transfer's recipient, clean in round 1, is now split into two byte pieces. canCall and the custom-error reverts are newly decoded.
